issues.description: The problem statement contains a conflicting parameter type for addGuestStudents: one sentence specifies addGuestStudents(String) while the UML and the intended implementation use addGuestStudents(int). This inconsistency can confuse students about which parameter type to implement and may lead to failing tests if they follow the incorrect String signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the problem statement to consistently specify addGuestStudents(int) as the required signature (matching the UML and solution). Ensure any textual mentions of addGuestStudents(String) are corrected to use the int parameter to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement text describes the method addGuestStudents with a parameter type of String ("addGuestStudents(String)"), while the UML diagram and the solution/template implementations use an int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)). This mismatch in the method signature across artifacts can confuse students about the expected parameter type, leading to incorrect implementations or compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across artifacts. Update the problem statement text to specify addGuestStudents(int) and describe that the method accepts an integer number of new guest students (e.g., change "addGuestStudents(String)" to "addGuestStudents(int)").
